text: which ever one you think will let me do like a chainlink fence style would be good
resolution: Built a parametric Lattice/grille primitive so chainlink fences (and the fence-top slot band the user hand-cut for 20 min) come from one Add instead of cutting + re-facing every opening by hand. New latticePanel() in editMesh.ts generates a thin walled panel from crossed bars — each a correctly-wound cuboid rotated and merged, so the inner walls of every hole exist for free. Pattern 'diamond' lays ±45 deg wires (chainlink); 'grid' lays axis-aligned mullions (slot bands, vents, railing infill). cols/rows = opening density, bar = wire width, frame = optional border; diagonal wires are clipped to panel bounds so nothing pokes out, and it stays light (a 4x2m chainlink ~324 faces, one box per bar not a quad per cell). Wired into the Add Shape dialog as a new Lattice shape with a pattern toggle + openings/wire/frame/thickness fields. Added 4 editMesh.test.ts suites (101/101 green) covering topology, bounds-clipping, density scaling, and the non-empty fallback; cart bundles clean via tsc-check.
